READING GUIDE

One observation.
Its own evidence.

Model identities, game outcomes and machine labels are deliberately absent. Start by reading, not by filling every box.

  1. Add an entry in the relevant field. A field can contain several entries: two conditions, several actions, different reasons. Keep distinct observations separate.
  2. Classify each entry. Check explicit advice, narrated event / belief, or both if the passage contains both. Use ambiguous when unclear. Narration is relevant evidence; it is not automatically a general recommendation.
  3. Attach its own quotations. Select words in a myth and click “Attach selected text” on the entry they support, or use “Paste quotation.” Each entry accepts several quotations. Check the source round when comparing earlier text.
  4. Capture reasons too. “Holding back would yield only a meager existence” expresses an expected consequence. It can go under rationale even though it does not directly prescribe an amount.
  5. Record absence and uncertainty. “Not specified” is valid and need not have an invented quotation. More imagery is not automatically a more complex strategy.
  6. Read all ten myths, then summarize. Use the bottom section for the whole trajectory. Compare earlier rounds before calling a rule new; record reversals and dropped rules.
The quotation check verifies wording, not whether it supports your interpretation. These notes do not establish that an agent followed a rule or that it caused cooperation.

Older notes are preserved. Their shared quotation is kept under Other evidence, not automatically attached to each field. Notes remain browser-local drafts: export a JSON copy before changing browsers or clearing site data. Both old and new exports can be imported. The local preview and private hosted site have separate browser storage; export/import to move your work.

Import review notes?

Notes for the trajectories in this file will replace their current drafts. Other trajectories stay unchanged.

Remove this evidence?

This removes the selected entry or quotation from your draft. Exported copies are unaffected.
